highlights.description: Apple this week was sued over a reported "Hide My Email" flaw that could expose a user's real email address. devices.description: Google and Epic Games this week withdrew their joint motion to modify an injunction requiring Google to support third-party app stores in Google Play. The two companies abandoned the request after it became clear the court was unlikely to allow it. Google is now bound by a permanent injunction issued in October 2024 requiring it to allow alternative app stores on Android devices. crypto.description: Mac users should watch out for macOS malware called CrashStealer, according to Jamf Threat Labs. CrashStealer collects browser data, password manager data, cryptocurrency wallet extensions, and keychain data, and Jamf first noticed it circulating in a fake Apple-notarized app called Werkbit. ev_autonomous.title: Tesla finally launches a bike — but it’s not what fans wanted
ev_autonomous.description: Tesla fans have spent years begging the company to build an e-bike. Tesla just launched a bike — and it has no motor, no pedals, and it’s for toddlers. The new “Balance Bike for Kids” sells for $225 on Tesla’s online shop, and it’s aimed at children aged 2 to 5.
